newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Strauss-Kahn repeats audit unlikely to be good.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn repeats audit unlikely to be good.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn repeated on Monday that the results of an audit of public finances were unlikely to be very good.
The audit, being carried out by two members of the independent Court of Auditors, is due on July 21.
"We are awaiting the results of the audit. I know that probably it will not be very good," Strauss-Kahn told a news conference after a meeting of European finance ministers.
"We will undoubtedly be forced to take some action," he added.

France's new Socialist-led government has said it will implement measures to reduce the budget deficit if the audit shows it significantly overshooting Maastricht treaty requirements to cut it to, or towards three percent of gross domestic product.
Strauss-Kahn said last week the deficit was likely to be significantly higher than the 3.0 percent of gross domestic product forecast by the previous centre-right government in the 1997 Finance Act.
"A large part of these difficulties is due to revenues which are lower than expected," he said on Monday. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
